title: Hi, there, welcome to my page!
text:
Research profile
My current research investigates how syntactic, semantic, and discourse-related factors affect direct object realisation in Spanish.
When it comes to methods, I combine corpus-based and experimental approaches, such as custom corpus compilation, acceptability judgements, elicitation, and eye-tracking. Drawing on natural language processing methods and statistical modelling, I analyse linguistic variation quantitavely with the goal of identifying common patterns across speakers.
More broadly, I am interested in how empirical linguistic data can be used to explain language variation, second language acquisition, and general linguistic processing.

title: Hi, there, welcome to my page!
text:
Current research activities


SFB Language between Redundancy and Deficiency
2024 – present


Subproject 07 · Deficiency and Redundancy in Ibero-Romance pronominal systems

My current work examines patterns of pronominal object realisation using experimental and corpus-linguistic evidence from Spain, Portugal, Brazil and Argentina.
The project includes the development and implementation of acceptability, elicitation and eye-tracking experiments, as well as the statistical analysis of cross-linguistic and cross-varietal data.

title: Talks
text:
Entre omisión y doblado – variación en la realización del objeto directo en español y portugués
Date: 2026
Venue: Graz (Austria) Event: Tribuna Festival (Universität Graz)
Presentation of null objects and clitic doubling as our phenomena of interest and the fieldwork experiments conducted in our subproject; discussion of the first results of our cross-variety null object experiments.
Download presentation (PDF)


Predicting null objects – a quantitative perspective on direct object realisation patterns in Peninsular Spanish
Date: 2026
Venue: Zürich (Switzerland) Event: Linguistisches Kolloquium (Universität Zürich)
Presentation of existing analyses of null objects in Peninsular Spanish and contextualisation in light of first empirical results from experiments and a corpus study (sampled from Youtube podcasts). Discussion of ellipsis approaches to Spanish object omission based on information-structural and pragmatic constraints.
Download presentation (PDF)


Predicting Direct Object Omission - A Quantitative Approach to Direct Object Realisation Patterns in Contemporary Peninsular Spanish
Date: 2026
Venue: Kandersteg (Switzerland) Event: Alpes 6 (Universität Zürich)
This talk focuses on the construction of a corpus specifically designed for the analysis of null objects in Spanish. The study addresses criteria for data selection, annotation, and corpus exploitation, with the aim of identifying systematic patterns of direct object omission and assessing the linguistic factors that condition their distribution.
Download presentation (PDF)


Verb-driven Patterns of Object Omission in the History of Spanish: A Corpus-based Analysis
Date: 2025
Venue: Universitat de les Illes Balears (Palma, Spain)
Event: Null Objects from a Crosslinguistic and Developmental Perspective
This poster presentation gives insights into an ongoing diachronic corpus study of direct object omission in Spanish, based on a newly compiled and annotated corpus of texts from the 12th to the 18th century. It investigates whether verb classes and lexical semantics can predict patterns of null object realization, and evaluates these findings in relation to clitic doubling and existing diachronic accounts.
Download presentation (PDF)


Un análisis de corpus sobre el marcado diferencial de objeto en hablantes de L2 español con L1 alemán
Date: 2025
Venue: Bergische Universität Wuppertal (Wuppertal, Germany)
Event: Invited Talk at Jornadas Lingüísticas BUW
This talk presents a corpus-based study of the acquisition of Differential Object Marking (DOM) in L2 Spanish by L1 German speakers, comparing learner and native usage. Using multifactorial random forest analyses, it examines the relative impact of semantic, pragmatic, and verbal factors on DOM realisation and omission.
Download presentation (PDF)


Empirical Perspectives on the Object Agreement Cycle analysis of different varieties of Spanish
Date: 2025
Venue: University of Hamburg (Hamburg, Germany)
Event: Deutscher Hispanistentag: Sektion zum Status des Dativs
This talk investigates clitic doubling and null objects in Spanish from a diachronic corpus perspective, critically evaluating the Object Agreement Cycle. Drawing on historical data from multiple varieties, it shows that null objects precede and compete with clitic doubling, challenging strictly sequential accounts of object realisation.

title: Publications
text:
Differential object marking in the L2 Spanish of L1 German speakers: A corpus-based analysis (2024)
In: Jonas Grünke, Andrea Pešková & Christoph Gabriel (eds.), Spanish as a second and third language: Approaching the linguistics-didactics interface, 39–69. Berlin: Frank & Timme GmbH.
DOI: 10.57088/978-3-7329-8970-6_3



Abstract


El presente estudio contribuye a la investigación de la adquisición
del marcado diferencial de objeto (ingl. differential object marking,
DOM) del español como segunda lengua (L2), evaluando cuantitativamente
el uso escrito del DOM por hablantes nativos de español europeo y por
parte de hablantes de alemán como lengua primera (L1). Mediante un
enfoque basado en corpus, se analizan más de 100 textos escritos en
términos de la alternancia a/∅ con objetos directos nominales,
evaluando un conjunto de predictores semánticos y de estructura de la
información utilizando un análisis multifactorial basado en
clasificaciones de bosques aleatorios. Con este enfoque se investiga
hasta qué punto y en función de qué factores el grupo de hablantes L2
difiere del grupo nativo en su uso del DOM.
